nodes.name: NSC synthesis
nodes.procedure: A mixture of 1.8 g of melamine, 0.6 g of glucose and 6 mg of sulfur powder was ground in a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene ball mill tube at a frequency of 50 Hz for 20 minutes to ensure homogeneity. The white mixed powder was initially carbonized to 600 °C at a rate of 2.5 °C min⁻¹ using the tube furnace under the Ar atmosphere and held for an additional 30 minutes, then ramped up to 900 °C at the same rate for 60 minutes. The obtained sample was named NSC after cooling to room temperature.

nodes.name: Pt/NSC impregnation reduction
nodes.procedure: 50 mg of NSC carbon material was placed in a 25 mL beaker, 750 μL of H2PtCl6·6H2O aqueous solution (50 mM) and 250 μL of deionized water were added, ultrasonic dispersed for 30 minutes, and dried in an oven at 45 °C. After the obtained black powder sample was calcinated to 600 °C for 120 minutes in Ar atmosphere at a calcinating reduction rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ and then naturally cooled to room temperature, it was marked with Pt/NSC.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM image of Pt/NSC shows three-dimensional layered structure with rough and porous surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microstructure and crystal structure of the Pt/NSC are characterized by field emission scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The SEM image of NSC (Fig. 2a) visually illustrates a three-dimensional layered structure with a rough and porous surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Pt/NSC has Pt NPs with average diameter of 1.68 nm uniformly dispersed; Pt/NC shows larger 2.43 nm particles with uneven distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image of Pt/NSC (Fig. 2b) reveals that Pt NPs with an average diameter of 1.68 nm, are uniformly dispersed across the wrinkled carbon layer that formed by the stacking of carbon layers. In contrast, TEM images of Pt/NC (Fig. S2†) demonstrate the uneven distribution of the particles, with a larger average particle size of 2.43 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows well-defined lattice fringes with spacing of 0.227 nm corresponding to (111) plane of fcc Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) image (Fig. 2c) reveals well-defined lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.227 nm, which corresponds to the (111) plane of face-centered cubic (fcc) Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern displays symmetrically distributed Pt cluster with bright diffraction spots and continuous ring for amorphous carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 2d) displays a symmetrically distributed Pt cluster characterized by bright diffraction spots, alongside a continuous ring that signifies the typical diffraction pattern associated with amorphous carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image and C, N, Pt, S elemental mapping confirm homogeneous distribution and successful incorporation of N and S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image and C, N, Pt, and S element mapping images of Pt/NSC (Fig. 2e–i).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines Pt content in Pt/NSC as 7.67 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt content in the Pt/NSC is quantitatively determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), yielding a result of 7.67% (Table S1†).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows broad C (002) peak at ~22°; Pt/NC exhibits Pt (111) peak at 39.6° but Pt/NSC shows no Pt peaks due to small particle size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 3a, a prominent broad peak at approximately 22° corresponds to the diffraction peak of the C (002) crystal plane of the carbon material. The Pt/NC sample exhibits a distinct diffraction peak near 39.6°, which is attributed to the fcc (111) crystal plane of Pt. In contrast, diffraction peaks associated with Pt are not observed in Pt/NSC...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D-band at 1350 cm⁻¹ and G-band at 1592 cm⁻¹; ID/IG = 0.97 for Pt/NSC (lower than Pt/NC's 1.00) indicating enhanced graphitization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic Raman peaks observe at approximately 1350 cm⁻¹ and 1592 cm⁻¹ for Pt/NSC and Pt/NC in Fig. 3b... The ID/IG value for Pt/NSC (0.97) is slightly lower than that of Pt/NC (1.00)...

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms show Pt/NSC surface area 402.99 m²/g (vs Pt/NC 378.6 m²/g) with type IV isotherm indicating mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The analytical calculations based on the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) method reveal that Pt/NSC possesses a specific surface area of 402.99 m² g⁻¹, higher than that of Pt/NC (378.6 m² g⁻¹). Meanwhile, Pt/NSC displays a type IV isotherm with a pronounced hysteresis loop...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Pt,C,N,O,S presence; S 2p (0.28 wt%) shows negative shift; Pt 4f peaks at 71.31/74.75 eV (Pt⁰) with 0.14 eV negative shift vs Pt/NC; N 1s shows Pt-N at 399.53 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey XPS spectrum of Pt/NSC (Fig. S6†) confirms the presence of Pt, C, N, O, and S... XPS analysis of the Pt 4f region for Pt/NSC reveals two prominent peaks at 71.31 eV and 74.75 eV... The Pt 4f peaks of Pt/NSC slightly shift towards lower binding energies by 0.14 eV compared to Pt/NC...
